t: New York, nineteen oh six. The best cook in town carries a deadly secret.
Wherever Mary Mallon cooks, people get typhoid.
A banker's summer house. Six of eleven fall sick.
An investigator, George Soper, tracks down her old jobs.
Seven families. Twenty-two cases. One cook.
Miss Mallon, I'll need samples. Of... everything.
She chases him out with a carving fork.
Then the police come. Mary hides for five hours.
The tests are clear. She's full of typhoid germs.
(angry) I've never been sick a day in my life!
True. She's a healthy carrier. The first one found in America.
The papers call her Typhoid Mary. And they lock her on an island.
Three years later, she's freed. On one condition: no more cooking.
So she becomes Mary Brown. A cook. At a maternity hospital.
Back to the island. For twenty-three years. Until she dies.
